findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether self-heal alone satisfies the recurrence-prevention goal, or whether it is a recovery half that must be paired with the deferred load-side lever (admission/concurrency bound or capacity) tracked in inherited-americium-porpoise — and address the case where the healed replacement is itself OOM-killed or the below-floor memory abort refuses to start it under continuing gate load.
evidence: Plan: 'implement enough that /mcp cannot remain pinned to a dead backend after gate-induced MCP failure.'
Parent 9ea3 verifier blocker: 'memory oversubscription under concurrent gates is not bounded by admission control, instance sizing, or off-box execution'

Parent RCA comment: '~10 concurrent x ~739 MB + 2.17 GB steady = ~9.6 GB demand against an 8 GiB host' — the OOM is load-driven, and 'A per-container mem_limit alone does not fix this ... The load-side control is the missing lever.'
autodeploy.sh:1135-1141 memory floor aborts starting a second container when MemAvailable < MCP_MEM_MIN_MB — i.e. exactly under the pressure that killed the first
findings.finding: The self-heal recovers the serving path after an MCP death but does not bound the recurrence driver the parent verifier named (memory oversubscription under ~10 concurrent gates); the replacement is started on the same box under the same pressure, so it can be OOM-killed in turn or be refused by the very memory floor it honors, leaving /mcp 502 until pressure abates.
findings.location: RCA / design decision section; Acceptance Criteria AC2/AC4
scenarios: Concurrent gate load OOM-kills the live MCP; self-heal starts a replacement that is itself killed under continuing load, or the below-floor memory abort refuses to start it — /mcp stays 502 across multiple ticks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify which image reference the self-heal passes when reusing mcp_run_new (the currently-deployed SHA tag, not $TARGET) and how that tag is guaranteed to exist locally when a source change is pending on the same tick.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:686 mcp_run_new ends with `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — keyed on the fetch target SHA, not the deployed SHA.
Plan: self-heal 'runs on every tick before ordinary source-change deploy decisions' and starts 'from the currently deployed MCP image'.
MCP_PREV_SHA_FILE / mcp_deployed exist in the deploy path but mcp_run_new does not consume them.
findings.finding: The plan says the self-heal starts a replacement 'from the currently deployed MCP image', but the existing helper mcp_run_new starts `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` (the git-tip SHA). On a tick where a source change is pending ($TARGET != deployed), running before ordinary deploy decisions means the deployed image tag — not $TARGET — must be used, and $MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET may not have been built yet; the plan does not specify which image ref the heal passes to mcp_run_new.
findings.location: RCA / design decision step 3 ('start a replacement from the currently deployed MCP image')
scenarios: Live MCP dies while origin/main has advanced; the heal fires before the source-change build, but mcp_run_new would tag $TARGET, whose image is not built — the heal fails to start a replacement, or (worse) reuses a wrong image ref.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL is wired to an operator-visible metric/alarm as-code (observability.sh delta publish + a monitoring_*.tf CloudWatch alarm) like the sibling MCP markers, or justify why a bare journald marker satisfies AC3; if a metric/alarm is added, reconcile that with the plan's claim that no Terraform apply is required.
evidence: Plan step 5: "emit countable journal markers (`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL` plus existing error markers on failure)"
monitoring_foxterrier.tf wires each existing marker to rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap / mcp_mem_abort via observability.sh §4f plus a metric alarm on the SNS alerts topic

Parent ticket's retire-sweep decision reused AUTODEPLOY_ERROR precisely because a fresh token "would have needed its own `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` call, an offset file, and a terraform metric before it was visible at all"
AC3 requires "an operator-visible metric/log/alarm"
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new countable journal marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL to satisfy AC3's operator-visible-signal requirement, but does not specify whether it is wired through the established as-code observability contract (observability.sh publish_autodeploy_marker_delta + a Terraform CloudWatch metric alarm) the way the sibling AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP / AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT markers are — while simultaneously asserting no Terraform apply is required unless HCL changes emerge. As written, the self-heal event may be only a bare journald line, not an operator-visible metric/alarm reproducible as-code.
findings.location: RCA/design decision step 5 (`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL`) and Testing/verification plan ("no Terraform alarm apply is required unless HCL changes emerge")
scenarios: A self-heal fires in production but no CloudWatch metric/alarm exists, so an operator only sees it if they grep the on-box journal — matching this incident's original failure mode where the box's logs are journald-only and lost with the host
A repeated self-heal loop (thrashing between promote and reap) produces no paging signal because the new marker was never given a metric filter
findings.suggested_fix: Either reuse the existing AUTODEPLOY_ERROR/deploy_errors path (as the parent's retire-sweep fix did) so the self-heal is countable without new HCL, or add a rebar/host:mcp_self_heal delta publish in observability.sh plus a CloudWatch alarm in monitoring_9ea3.tf and update the verification plan to include that Terraform apply.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for the readiness/nginx-failure heal arm: replacement fails a cutover gate, assert it is removed only if it never served, the dead live backend is retained, an error marker is emitted, and the next tick retries (plus a case for the unreadable-memory fail-open path).
evidence: Testing plan enumerates only: RED test for successful flip+reap, and 'Companion test covers low-memory self-heal refusal'

Remediation note: 'a started replacement that fails /health, store readiness, startup handshake, nginx -t, or reload is removed if it never served, the dead live backend is retained ... the normal MCP backoff makes the next attempt retryable rather than terminal.' — a designed failure arm with no listed test
findings.finding: The testing plan lists only two cases (successful self-heal, low-memory refusal) but the design explicitly defines a distinct readiness/nginx-failure disposition arm — a replacement that starts but fails /health, store readiness, startup handshake, `nginx -t`, or reload must be removed if it never served, the dead live backend retained, an error marker emitted, and the next attempt made retryable via backoff. No test exercises this arm, nor the unreadable-memory fail-open path.
findings.location: Testing / verification plan; 'Readiness/nginx failure disposition' remediation note
findings.suggested_fix: Extend test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py with a case where the started replacement fails /health or nginx reload, asserting: dead live backend retained, replacement reaped, error marker emitted, upstream unchanged, and next-tick retryability.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Rejected alternatives / prior-art section, address Docker's own restart policy: explain why the existing `--restart always` on the retained dead live container (autodeploy.sh:656) does not recover it and clear the 502, and why a bespoke blue/green self-heal is required instead of relying on or tuning that policy (and its health-check/backoff behavior).
evidence: Plan lists rejected alternatives (nginx multi-upstream/failover, instance sizing, off-box gates, passive max_fails/fail_timeout+backup) but never mentions Docker restart policy.
Codebase: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:656 `--restart always` is already set on MCP containers via mcp_run_new().

Codebase comment autodeploy.sh:737-738: prior 502 was because a crashed live container was `docker rm`'d so `--restart always` 'then had nothing left to restart' — implying restart-in-place is the intended recovery once the container is retained.
Plan premise: 'If the container is exited/OOM-killed and Docker does not restart it promptly' — acknowledges the restart policy exists but does not explain its inadequacy.

Web prior art (retrieved DuckDuckGo results): 'Docker Restart Policies and Health Checks', 'Fix Docker: OOM killed container', 'bhived: 502 Bad Gateway OOM-killed upstream — Restart the live app container' all treat container restart policy/`docker restart` as the standard OOM self-heal.
findings.finding: The prior-art / rejected-alternatives section does not consider Docker's own container restart policy (`--restart always`/`on-failure`) as the first-line self-heal for an OOM-killed/exited backend, even though the codebase already runs MCP containers with `--restart always` (autodeploy.sh:656) and the plan's own recurrence premise is that 'Docker does not restart it promptly.' Without analyzing why the existing restart policy fails to recover the retained dead live container, the novel blue/green self-heal path is not justified against the established, already-present prior art.
findings.location: RCA / design decision -> 'Rejected alternatives'; Plan-review remediation notes
scenarios: An MCP container is OOM-killed while retained as the live backend; a reviewer/operator asks why `--restart always` (already configured) does not simply bring the same container back and clear the 502, rather than requiring a whole new blue/green promotion.
The failure is actually a Docker restart-backoff or an exit-0 that `--restart always` does not retry, in which case tuning the restart policy could be the smaller, established fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rejected-alternative entry: 'Docker restart policy (`--restart always`, already set on MCP containers): does not recover the serving path because <specific reason — e.g., restart backoff caps / clean exit not retried / restarted process comes up but stalls at store-readiness or startup-handshake so nginx stays pinned>. Therefore in-place restart cannot guarantee a live, ready backend on the served port, which the blue/green promotion + readiness gates + atomic flip do.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Weigh and record the disposition of an in-place `docker restart` of the dead live container (keeps name+port, nginx include stays valid, no second-container memory overlap) against the chosen blue/green self-heal, since it is the manual recovery already proven on-box in the parent.
evidence: Parent 9ea3 comments: 'I used docker restart rather than remove-and-recreate specifically so the container kept its name and nginx's upstream include stayed valid' — verified recovery with no upstream flip needed.

Plan starts a SECOND container (steps 3-5) which is gated by the memory floor (autodeploy.sh:1138) precisely when memory is scarce; an in-place restart reuses the existing port/name and needs no 2x overlap.
Rejected-alternatives list covers only nginx multi-upstream, instance sizing, and off-box — not in-place restart.
findings.finding: A structurally simpler recovery alternative — an in-place `docker restart` of the dead live container (which keeps its name and port so the nginx include stays valid) — was neither considered nor rejected, despite being the exact manual recovery already proven on-box twice in the parent and avoiding the second-container memory 2x overlap, free-port selection, and name-collision handling the chosen heal introduces.
findings.location: RCA / design decision -> Rejected alternatives; Plan-review remediation notes
scenarios: Under memory pressure, a blue/green heal is refused by the memory floor while an in-place restart of the crashed container (no overlap, same port) would have restored serving.

No feature flag, staged enablement, or explicit rollback statement is given; live verification only observes recovery
